newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran begins amphibious wargames in Gulf on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Iran begins amphibious wargames in Gulf on Tuesday.

text.p: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards begin amphibious wargames in the Gulf on Tuesday to train for surprise attacks, Iran's official news agency IRNA said.

It quoted the guards' deputy commander Brigadier General Rahim Safavi as saying 200,000 troops would take part in the exercises code-named "Tariq-ol Qods" (Road to Jerusalem) set to open in the southern province of Bushehr.
The troops, including volunteer Bassij forces, would test surface-to-air, shore-to-sea and surface-to-surface missiles during the three-day games.
Iran said last week its army would hold amphibious exercises in the Gulf to train for surprise attacks against "enemies" posing threats to the Islamic Republic.

IRNA quoted Safavi as saying Iran, which holds wargames in the Gulf regularly, wanted "to upgrade the quality of its personnel so that it can better defend Islamic ideals and safeguard territorial integrity".

He stressed that security in the Gulf was a collective responsibility "of all regional countries and as such Iran is holding the Tariq-ol Qods manoeuvres as a step to demonstrate its prowess for guaranteeing Persian Gulf security".
He said his country would not allow any "alien power to destabilise regional security".
Safavi said the departure of the "intruding forces" -- a term often used in Iran to describe U.S. forces in the Gulf -- would help enhance cooperation among regional states.
